texts.orig: The confinement of quarks in hadrons occurs due to formation of QCD string: At separation between the quarks the QCD string breaks into pieces due to light  quark-antiquark pair creation We argue that there exist a critical background magnetic field eB ~ 16m? _ above which the breaking is impossible in the transverse  directions with respect to the axis of the magnetic field. Thus; at strong enough magnetic field a new, asymmetrically confining phase may form The effect which can potentially be tested at LHC/ALICE experiment leads to abundance of u-quark rich hadrons and to excess of radially excited mesons in the noncentral heavy-ion collisions compared to the central ones large string
